chain.label: Pilot's limited recent experience in the demanding Nimbus-4DM
chain.trigger: The check pilot stated “it takes a lifetime to learn to fly this type of sailplane [Nimbus-4DM]....”; the pilot had 103 hours in type over 3 years and only 8 hours in six flights in the 1999 season before the accident, and the rear-seat occupant had flown the type only once.

chain.label: Strong unstable thermal/turbulent convective conditions
chain.trigger: “Atmosphere unstable over Western Nevada... Today will be hot and good thermal activity will result” (soaring index 1,756 fpm); a witness in another glider reported “it was very turbulent and there were a lot of updrafts and downdrafts present.”

chain.label: Departure from controlled flight into a spiral/spin while thermalling
chain.trigger: “the accident glider was in a tight turn, as if climbing in a thermal, when it entered the spiral”; the glider was seen in a high-speed spiral with a 45-degree nose-down attitude.

caused_by.evidence: The glider “was particularly sensitive to over input of the rudder control during turns with a resulting tendency for unwanted rolling moments,” and the pilot had flown little in type recently.
“The glider broke up in flight during the recovery phase after a departure from controlled flight while maneuvering in thermal lift conditions.”

chain.label: Rapid airspeed buildup in steep descending spiral toward/beyond Vne
chain.trigger: “With a 45-degree nose-down attitude, the speed quickly built up as the glider completed two full rotations”; the manufacturer computed acceleration from Vs to Vne in 8.6 seconds and Vne to Vd in another 1.8 seconds at that attitude.

caused_by.evidence: The uncontrolled 45-degree nose-down spiral produced the rapid acceleration; “the nose pitched further down to a near-vertical attitude.”

chain.label: Airbrakes extended at high speed during the dive recovery
chain.trigger: “Detailed examination of witness marks and other evidence in the wreckage established that the pilot extended the airbrakes at some point in an attempt to slow the glider during the descent prior to the breakup.”

caused_by.evidence: Airbrakes “should only be used at such high speeds in emergency or if the maximum permitted speeds are being exceeded inadvertently” — the pilot deployed them to arrest the overspeed.

chain.label: Abrupt nose-up elevator pullout above maneuvering speed
chain.trigger: “The glider was observed to level its attitude, with the wings bending upward and the wing tips coning higher” after the near-vertical dive; the AFM warns “Avoid especially sudden elevator control movements” and permits full control deflection only at or below Va (97 kts).

caused_by.evidence: The pullout was the response to the near-vertical, high-speed descent.

Certification flight test data showed “the elevator control stick forces were relatively light, with only 11.9 pounds of force (nosedown) required to hold a fixed attitude at Vne,” a handling trait demanding familiarity with the type.

chain.label: Wing loading driven well beyond ultimate design load
chain.trigger: “All the wing failures were overload in character and occurred at loadings well above the ultimate design load limits”; witnesses estimated wing deflection reached 45 degrees or more, matching the 46.5-degree ultimate-load deflection.

caused_by.evidence: The pullout at high speed generated the positive bending that deflected the wings upward and coned the tips.

“the airbrakes function like spoilers and have the effect of shifting the aerodynamic loads outboard on the wings,” and with airbrakes/flaps extended at Vne the positive load limit drops from 5.3 to 3.5 g.

chain.label: Symmetrical overload failure of both outboard wing sections
chain.trigger: “the left and right wings had failed symmetrically, in overload, at two distinct locations common to the outboard wing sections”; NIAR determined Section EE was most likely the first failure, with skin buckling preceding spar failure.

caused_by.evidence: “Compressive failure at the top and tensile failures at the bottom is consistent with an upward deflection and failure of the wing tip section,” with the structure loaded beyond ultimate.

chain.label: In-flight breakup of the glider
chain.trigger: “The outboard wing tip panels departed from the glider, the wings disintegrated, and the fuselage dove into the ground.”

caused_by.evidence: Dynamic response after the first spar failure produced the subsequent failures; about 26 feet of outer wing per side separated and was found up to 0.5 mile from the main crash site.

chain.label: Fuselage impacted terrain in an uncontrolled dive
chain.trigger: “The fuselage mass impact created a crater that measured approximately 8 feet long by 6 feet wide,” about 4 statute miles from the Minden-Tahoe Airport.

caused_by.evidence: With the wings disintegrated, “the fuselage dove into the ground.”

chain.label: Both occupants fatally injured
chain.trigger: “The commercial glider pilot and a passenger were fatally injured, and the glider was destroyed.”

caused_by.evidence: “the cause of death for both the pilot and passenger were blunt-force trauma, without contributing preexisting conditions”; no parachute deployment was observed.
